p1.title: Passage 1
paras: The New Education Policy (NEP) introduced in India seeks to reform the traditional education structure by emphasizing flexibility, multidisciplinary learning, and skill development. Unlike earlier systems that largely prioritized rote memorization and examination performance, the NEP advocates conceptual understanding, creativity, and critical thinking. The policy also proposes integrating vocational education and digital technology into mainstream learning. Supporters argue that such reforms can better prepare students for the demands of a rapidly changing global economy. However, critics contend that implementation remains a major challenge, especially in rural and economically disadvantaged regions where infrastructure, trained faculty, and digital access are limited. Concerns have also been expressed regarding linguistic diversity and the practical feasibility of certain policy recommendations. Despite these debates, many educational experts consider the NEP one of the most ambitious reforms attempted in recent decades. Its long-term success will ultimately depend on effective administration, teacher preparedness, and equitable access to educational resources.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: Cricket in modern India has evolved from a leisurely sport into a complex social and economic institution. Its growing popularity has been fueled by mass media, corporate sponsorships, and franchise-based leagues. Financial investment has improved infrastructure and global visibility, but it has also altered priorities within the game. Player selection and retention are increasingly influenced by market value and audience appeal. Technological tools such as performance analytics and video reviews have enhanced accuracy while intensifying scrutiny. Constant evaluation places psychological pressure on players and shortens professional careers. Traditional ideals of patience, sportsmanship, and long-term development often conflict with expectations of instant success. Despite these tensions, cricket continues to function as a powerful unifying force across regions and classes. Thus, the sport reflects a delicate balance between emotional attachment and commercial ambition.
